title: Cap. VI Arg. 2 close: faith-bearing grace given by freest will — so predestination unbound to prior free-choice acts
pass_a_gloss: Since therefore this special and efficacious grace which brings forth faith, and conversion, does not prerequire an antecedent condition of our faith, but is given to certain ones, not given to others, according to the freest will of the one giving or not-giving; it is plain that predestination itself, which is the cause of such grace prepared and gifted, is not bound to any antecedent acts of human choice, but is constituted in the free good pleasure of God himself, according to that of the Apostle, I will have mercy on whom I will have had mercy, Rom. 9:15.
pass_b_english: So this special efficacious grace that brings forth faith and conversion does not prerequire an antecedent condition of our faith — it is given to some and not to others by the freest will of the Giver. Plainly then predestination itself, the cause of such grace prepared and gifted, is not bound to any antecedent acts of human choice, but is constituted in God's free good pleasure — per Rom. 9:15, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy.
source_text: Quandoquidem igitur haec specialis et efficax gratia quae fidem parit, et conversionem, non praerequirit antecedaneam fidei nostrae conditionem, sed datur quibusdam, aliis non datur, pro liberrima dantis aut non-dantis voluntate; manifestum est ipsam praedestinationem, quae est causa talis gratiae praeparatae et donatae, non esse alligatam actibus ullis antecedaneis humani arbitrii, sed constitutam in gratuito beneplacito ipsius Dei, juxta illud Apostoli, Miserebor cujus misertus fuero, Rom. ix. 15.
